sources.label: Dreamcore — Archon Tornado Acolyte of Chayula

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The Archon Tornado build runs on the Acolyte of Chayula, a hidden Monk ascendancy unlocked through the Breach questline. Its signature is a Tornado trigger chain: you seed Tornadoes that repeatedly trigger a damage spell (often a fire 'Molten Shower' style effect), and the build scales that chain by stacking Strength.
This is advanced and gates on a hidden-unlock step most players miss. The payoff is a screen-wide, mostly passive damage field that also performs on bosses if you position the Tornadoes well.

sections.title: Pros and Cons
pros: Tornado chain deals passive, screen-wide damage once seeded.
Strength stacking scales the whole chain from one attribute.
Performs in both maps and boss arenas with good positioning.
Hidden ascendancy feels rewarding once unlocked.
cons: Requires the hidden Breach unlock most players skip.
Advanced to pilot — Tornado placement and trigger uptime need practice.
Strength-stacking gear can get expensive at the top end.
If the chain drops, you are a weak monk with no clear.

sections.title: Is This Build Right For You?
paragraphs: Pick this if you enjoy trigger/DoT playstyles, do not mind a hidden-unlock detour, and want a Strength-scaling caster. If you want a straightforward league starter, pick a more direct Monk build.
You must complete the Breach questline to ascend Acolyte of Chayula. It is not available from the normal ascendancy choice, so budget the unlock into your plan.

steps.label: Campaign — Any Monk Skill
body: Level with a generic Monk skill (Tempest Flurry or Twister). Do not chase the Tornado chain before the hidden unlock.

steps.label: Breach Unlock — Acolyte of Chayula
body: Complete the Breach questline to gain the Acolyte of Chayula ascendancy. This is the gate; nothing else matters until it is done.

steps.label: Early Maps — Tornado Chain
body: Seed Tornadoes and build the trigger chain once you have the ascendancy and a Strength base.

sections.title: The Hidden Acolyte of Chayula Unlock
paragraphs: Acolyte of Chayula is not on the normal ascendancy screen. You reach it by progressing the Breach questline — a sequence most campaign guides skip because it is off the main path. Until that quest is done, the ascendancy node simply is not offered.
Plan for it explicitly. Players who 'could not find the ascendancy' almost always skipped the Breach step. Treat the unlock as a prerequisite, not an afterthought.

skills.role: Seeds the trigger chain that repeats your damage spell
notes: Tornado placement is the skill — seed them on packs and on the boss hitbox.
whyUse: Tornado is the engine: it periodically re-triggers the linked spell, turning one cast into a sustained field.

skills.role: The spell the Tornado chain repeatedly fires
whyUse: The 'Molten Shower' effect is what the Tornado seeds repeatedly — stacked fire bursts that blanket the screen.
mappingBossingDiff: On maps it blankets packs; on bosses you seed directly on the hitbox for sustained single-target.

skills.role: Adds cold shatter synergy to the trigger chain
notes: Herald of Ice shatter adds a second layer of clear on top of the fire chain.
Drop the Bell on a boss to amp the seeded Tornadoes.

sections.title: Why Strength Stacking
paragraphs: The Acolyte of Chayula notable converts a portion of Strength into the scaling the Tornado chain uses. Because Strength also gives life and melee/attribute benefits, every point you invest does double duty: more damage and more survival. That is why the build funnels almost everything into Strength.
The trap is splitting attributes. If you dilute into Dexterity or Intelligence, the chain loses the Strength multiplier and feels weak. Stack Strength, then fix resistances and life from gear.

sections.title: Mapping Loop
paragraphs: Seed Tornadoes across the pack as you move, let the chain fire the Molten Shower effect passively, and keep Herald of Ice shatter cleaning up. You are planting, not casting — the screen clears itself.

sections.title: Boss Loop
paragraphs: Seed Tornadoes directly on the boss hitbox, drop Tempest Bell, and let the chain hammer the same spot. Against movers, predict the path and pre-seed where they will stand, just like any ground-effect build.

steps.label: Why Acolyte of Chayula
body: Its notable converts Strength into Tornado-chain scaling — the exact multiplier this build needs. No other Monk ascendancy fuels the chain this way.

steps.label: Strength Clusters
body: Path through Strength notables that also give life. Avoid attributes you do not scale.

steps.label: Trigger / Area
body: Grab area and trigger-frequency notables to widen and speed the chain.

recommendations: A quarterstaff with added damage and Strength. The weapon mostly enables the chain; damage comes from Strength.
notes: Strength here is the damage lever, not weapon DPS.

statPriorities.label: Added Damage
statPriorities.reason: Flat value on top of Strength.

recommendations: Life and resistances first; an armour/evasion base that also gives Strength is ideal.

statPriorities.label: Life
statPriorities.reason: Strength already helps; life is the floor.

recommendations: Jewels granting Strength and life. A Strength jewel is the single biggest chain multiplier.
notes: Stack Strength jewels until the chain feels topped out.

statPriorities.label: Strength + Life
statPriorities.reason: Damage and survival from one jewel.

priorities.label: Strength
priorities.reason: The core multiplier for the whole Tornado chain.

priorities.label: Life
priorities.reason: Strength gives some, but cap it from gear.

priorities.label: Resistances
priorities.reason: Mandatory floor before any damage mods.

steps.label: 1 — Hidden Unlock
body: Complete the Breach questline for Acolyte of Chayula. Nothing else matters until this is done.

steps.label: 2 — Strength Base
body: Get Strength high enough that the chain visibly scales. Do this before any unique.

steps.label: 3 — Trigger Supports
body: Spell Cascade and area supports widen the field.

steps.label: 4 — Luxury Strength Gear
body: Only after the core chain is stable.

sections.title: Defensive Layers
paragraphs: Defense comes from Strength-granted life plus the fact that you are planting Tornadoes at range, not standing in melee. Keep resistances capped and a life flask ready; the build is not a front-liner.
The biggest risk is over-investing in Strength and neglecting resistances, then dying to a single elemental hit. Balance the attribute with a resist/life floor.

sections.title: Community Questions

entries.label: Hidden unlock
entries.statement: Players who 'cannot find Acolyte of Chayula' skipped the Breach questline — it is not on the normal ascendancy screen.

entries.label: Strength scaling
entries.statement: The common answer is too little Strength — the chain scales off it, so dilute attributes elsewhere and stack Strength.

entries.label: Boss matchup
entries.statement: Players confirm it bosses if you seed Tornadoes on the hitbox and drop the Bell; movers need pre-seeding.

sections.note: Player reports are experience, not verified mechanics. Confirm the exact Breach unlock step and Strength conversion against the current client.

checks: You skipped the Breach questline. Progress it to unlock the hidden ascendancy.
Strength is too low or attributes are split. Stack Strength and fix resistances from gear.
You are not seeding on the hitbox. Plant Tornadoes directly on the boss and drop the Bell.

items.question: Is the Breach unlock required?
answer: Yes. Acolyte of Chayula is a hidden ascendancy reached only through the Breach questline. Without it, the build cannot function.

items.question: Why Strength and not Dexterity?
answer: The Acolyte notable converts Strength into the Tornado-chain multiplier. Diluting into other attributes weakens that conversion.

items.question: Can I league-start this?
answer: You level as a Monk, but the hidden unlock + Strength plan is an early-map build, not a campaign starter.
